newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria loses $25 mln US wheat import credit line.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria loses $25 mln US wheat import credit line.

text.p: Bulgaria lost a $25 million credit guarantee for the import of 120,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat after state-owned Bulbank refused to confirm the credit line on the grounds that the conditions were unfavourable, officials said on Tuesday.
"The credit line for this year is lost. It is not renewable," U.S. embassy agriculture adviser William Huth told Reuters.
Bulgaria, battling an acute grain shortage due to excessive exports last year, faces a poor harvest this year and will have to import large quantities of wheat.
Sofia closed the wheat import deal with the United States Agriculture Department in August, fulfilling the conditions of the agreement by naming an importing company and a local bank to service it.

"Bulbank found the conditions of the agreement unacceptable and did not open a credit line by the September 30 deadline," a Bulbank official, who declined to be named, told Reuters. He declined to elaborate.
"We fulfilled our part of the agreement. The final decision was with Bulbank, which apparently defends the interests of its shareholders," said agriculture ministry spokeswoman Rosa Trichkova.
Bulgaria's current wheat supplies stand at 130,000 tonnes, while domestic wheat consumption is 500,000 tonnes, said the agriculture ministry.
The country is currently negotiating wheat imports with Ukraine and Kazakhstan.
Bulgaria also hopes to negotiate an import deal for 150,000 tonnes of wheat with the European Union.
The agriculture ministry has said it expected to buy 1.2 million tonnes of wheat from local producers, although the country needs 1.6 million tonnes a year for domestic human consumption.
